Re-tiered 2026-08-16 per Jaideep's directive: all three scenarios are built on the Wynn-open demand environment, stated once as a plain planning assumption in the notes block (fn14) — no other timing language appears anywhere. Sources: ras-al-khaimah/REVENUE-STACK-RAS-AL-KHAIMAH.md (§9 re-tier is the current basis) + CREW-COST-RAS-AL-KHAIMAH.md + TOURISM-DEMAND-RAS-AL-KHAIMAH.md + AUTHORITY-MAP-RAS-AL-KHAIMAH.md + SPEED-RULES-RAS-AL-KHAIMAH.md. GEOMETRY-RAS-AL-KHAIMAH.json is NOT a content source — the sealed RAK set is contaminated (mis-geocoded Dubai/AD POIs) and is cited only as the contamination finding for Grok locale cleanup (#119). NO route_ids render or bind anywhere in this file; the network is the four journey-spine corridors with DERIVED-approximate distances (Al Marjan↔Al Hamra 4.0 nm · Mina Al Arab↔Corniche 10.0 · Al Marjan↔Corniche 17.0 · Creek↔Jazirat Al Hamra 13.0). CONTRACT v3: only `title` (<=6 words), `value`/figures, `note` (<=140 chars, partner-clean plain English), `status` (enum: market_priced | modeled | upside), and `fn` (footnote key) render — plus verbatim copy fields (headline/subline/body/chips/cards/quantity/price). Underscore-prefixed fields NEVER reach the DOM. null/missing = render nothing. Footnotes render ONCE in a single 'Notes & assumptions' section above the contact form. Fleet financing only — equity/fundraise/counterparty firewalls apply in full. Framing: three clean tiers on one planning basis — Conservative ~11.7 yr renders plainly as the deliberately thin floor, Mid ~3.8 yr is the working case, Upside ~2.9 yr adds the two upside-only lines (sponsorship, overnight cargo). The former base-destination tiering never renders and is preserved in _internal.superseded_2026_08_16. Calm frame: capital follows the destination's published growth (1.35M→3.5M visitors by 2030, $5.1B Wynn opening 2027) — growth-following language only. All scenario figures transcribed exactly from the worked revenue model (§9) and re-verified by script before writing. Demand pools are sourced visitor/development flows, labeled indicative — no employer trackers exist on this run and no employer page exists (international addendum). No phasing or fleet-count section: no sourced RAK fleet plan exists in the research set, so none renders.

fn1.text: Experience and charter pricing is positioned against Ras Al Khaimah's sourced water-leisure market: pearl-farm tours published at US$50–71 per person, mangrove kayaking at AED 100–175, the authority's heritage water line renting craft at AED 150 per 30 minutes and AED 300 per hour, and the AED 325 zipline as the emirate's marquee activity price. Published hourly charter rates above the heritage-craft tier are thin, so the charter band is a derived range with a conservative haircut.

fn2.text: Demand pool figures are indicative of demand potential along these corridors — sourced visitor flows and published development facts, not commitments or commercial relationships.

fn3.text: Economics are indicative ranges with conservative defaults. Upside lines — sponsorship and overnight cargo — are never included in base totals.

fn4.text: Ras Al Khaimah publishes no numeric waterway speed limits today. Every trip time on this page uses a conservative planning basis — slow near berths, in the creek and in the lagoons, 25 knots on the open coast, 20 knots after dark — and corridor distances are approximate, computed from real coordinates with over-water routing factors and rounded up. Final schedules are set with the transport authority under its 2026 marine regulation. The water line is never sold as faster than the road.

fn5.text: Committed-seat and spot pricing is a derived band, not a Ras Al Khaimah quote: anchored to the published street-taxi tariff, metered fares on these corridors, and a road-commute anchor of about AED 2,508 a month for Al Marjan to the city. Roads here are largely free-flowing, so pricing is positioned on arrival experience and direct resort-to-city hops, not time savings. Pending confirmation.

fn6.text: Crew costs use a UAE-adapted method: published UAE maritime wage surveys for a two-person crew (captain + deckhand), plus explicitly stated housing, transport, end-of-service, visa and medical allowances. The model uses $30 per hour loaded — the mid benchmark rounded up as a buffer. No emirate-specific wage rows were found, so UAE-wide benchmarks are used and labeled.

fn7.text: Spot-seat lines are computed as fill rate × residual commute seat-legs × fare, with seats sold rounded to whole seats; the stated seat count × fare is the exact revenue line.

fn8.text: The conservative case is deliberately thin: captured demand is held at the level of today's visitor base, and payback stretches well past typical financing horizons. It is shown plainly as the floor — not a financing case.

fn9.text: A 12-month operating year on a sheltered southern Gulf coast. June–September heat shifts midday sailings toward morning and evening slots; October–April is the event-season peak. Scenario counts are annual monthly averages with that shape absorbed.

fn10.text: Energy is priced at the published commercial electricity tariff for the northern emirates plus VAT — about $0.123 per kWh, applied at the top consumption slab to every kilowatt-hour as a conservative reading. At the program's standard $0.30 per kWh planning rate the energy line rises about 2.4×; the mid case stays cash-positive with payback moving to roughly 4.0 years.

fn11.text: All figures are US dollars. Local benchmarks are cited in UAE dirhams and convert at the pegged rate of 3.6725 dirhams per dollar.

fn12.text: Al Marjan Island has no public marine facility verified today. Its stop renders with that status stated: an interim landing coordinated through the operating yacht club's moorings, with the published Wynn Al Marjan marina (opening 2027) as the permanent landing.

fn13.text: Mina Al Arab's marina is developer-published and not independently verified as an operating facility; the Anantara resort on the lagoon operates today. The Jazirat Al Hamra waterfront has no verified marine facility and renders as a heritage-shore stop with that status stated.

fn14.text: Economics assume Wynn Al Marjan Island (opening 2027) is open.

_internal.sources: REVENUE-STACK-RAS-AL-KHAIMAH.md §9 re-tier (all layers, scenario tables, opex — script-verified sums). Crew: CREW-COST-RAS-AL-KHAIMAH.md (UAE-adapted method, LOW $21.47 / MID $27.97, model $30/hr). Energy: EtihadWE commercial top slab 38 fils + 5 fils surcharge = 43 fils/kWh + 5% VAT = 45.15 fils ÷ 3.6725 = $0.12294/kWh, marginal top-slab rate applied to ALL kWh (conservative; blended ~10% cheaper).

opex_basis.crew: Per-scenario activity hours × $30/hr: 209/246/263 hrs = $6,270/$7,380/$7,890; rendered as the band. Hours = (132 commute + sailings×1.25 + charter hrs) × 1.15 positioning-standby.
opex_basis.energy: 2,977/3,225/3,476 nm × 4.1 kWh/nm × $0.12294 = $1,501/$1,626/$1,752 per scenario; rendered as the band. Sensitivity at $0.30/kWh: line rises ~2.4×; Mid net falls ~$2.3K/mo, payback ~4.0 yr — stated in fn10.
opex_basis.maintenance: $82.5K/yr = $6,875/mo, program-consistent N45 figure, flat across scenarios.
opex_basis.berthing: $527/mo PRIMARY — Royal Yacht Club of RAK published rates, 39–48 ft wet berth 12-month rate AED 43/ft/mo incl. VAT × 45 ft = AED 1,935/mo ÷ 3.6725. Cheapest berth in the UAE run (AD $911 cross-check).
opex_basis.insurance: $4,167/mo ($50K/yr placeholder ≈ 2% hull + P&I; UAE-licensed insurer mandatory). Flagged for operator quotes.

_internal.opex_total_note: Opex varies by scenario (crew + energy scale with activity per the revenue-stack structure; fixed berth+insurance+maintenance = $11,569/mo): $19,340 / $20,575 / $21,211 — rendered as the conservative-to-upside band. Scenario nets reflect per-scenario opex; the Navier network share (10% of gross) scales with revenue per scenario.
_internal.network_share_basis: program standard: 10% of gross — $4,130 / $8,306 / $10,232.50 per scenario.

layer_pricing_basis.committed_bundles_L1: DERIVED band $400/$500/$650 per seat-month = 44 legs × spot × ~0.59 bundle discount ($389/$519/$649 rounded). Anchors: Al Marjan↔city metered taxi ≈ AED 57 (~$15.5, primary tariff math); Mina Al Arab↔city ≈ AED 34; abra AED 10/station public floor; road-commute anchor AED 2,508/mo (~$683). Re-tier: scenarios price at $500/$650/$650 with 24/32/36 seats — the $400 band floor is unused in the current tiering. 36 seats = the AD upside tier (stack §8 comparison row); the earlier reason for sitting below AD (thin commuter base) is directly addressed by the resort's published 9,000 jobs and 1,530 keys — flagged unproven. Status everywhere: modeled + fn5. Needs confirmation before external quoting.
layer_pricing_basis.spot_seats_L2: $20/$25/$25 per leg × 15/25/30% fill of residual seat-legs (2,464/2,112/1,936; residual = 3,520 − seats×44). Seats rounded to whole seats (370/528/580); seat count × fare is the exact line (fn7). 30% = the AD upside fill (stack §8 comparison row) — labeled unproven; no congestion driver in RAK.
layer_pricing_basis.experiences_charters_L3: Experiences 30/48/60 sailings at 12/14/14 pax, $45/$55/$55 pp vs sourced RAK band $27–88 (kayak/abra floor $27–48 · Suwaidi Pearls $50–71 · Jais Flight zipline anchor $88). 60 sailings/mo = 2/day = 840 pax/mo ≈ 1.3% of on-island occupied-room guests at the published resort scale (1,530 keys × 71.2% FY2024 occupancy × ~2 ≈ 2,180/day), excluding the rest of the 1.35M base and the seven operating hotels — conservative-fraction derivation. Charters 12/22/22 hrs at $475/$550/$550 — DERIVED from the AD adjacent-market band ($450–600) with a further haircut; only local published hourly is the RAKTA abra AED 300/hr (~$82, displacement heritage craft — floor, not comparator). Weakest-anchored price in this file — quantity deliberately not pushed in the top tier.
layer_pricing_basis.sponsorship_U1: $150K/yr fleet-level placeholder ÷ 4 vessels = $3,125/mo, program precedent. Upside only.
layer_pricing_basis.overnight_cargo_U2: 12 runs × $250 — courier-linehaul rate logic; no RAK waterborne freight tariff found ⇒ upside-only. Clean classes per the stack: resort resupply (Al Marjan/Al Hamra/Mina Al Arab), premium parcels, medical/lab specimens.

_internal.scenario_qa: Conservative ~11.7 yr is above the 10-yr financeable line — rendered plainly as the floor per the 2026-08-16 directive; inputs were NOT adjusted to fix it. Upside quantities sit at the AD tier ceilings (36 seats, 30% fill) and a two-a-day experience schedule (≈1.3% of on-island guests) — flagged unproven. Cross-city comparisons never render.

navier_intro.title: Meet the vessel

copy.headline: A U.S.-built electric hydrofoil.
copy.body: Navier is a U.S. builder of electric hydrofoil vessels. Its N45 Explorer carries 30 passengers at a foilborne cruise speed of about 20 knots — lifted clear of the water for a smooth ride above the wake and wash of conventional hulls. The smaller N30 Quanta carries 8. Foiling cuts energy use by up to ~90% versus a conventional planing hull, and both vessels run near-silent on electric power.
